growth_story.headline: Ethiopia's state-led boom gave way to war, debt distress and slower growth; since the birr was floated in 2024, growth has picked up again.
growth_story.arc: Income per person in Ethiopia fell 1.2 percent a year over 1990–1998, with deep drops in 1991 and 1992; the sources used here do not explain that era. Growth turned positive at 3.7 percent a year over 1999–2006 and then ran at 7.3 percent a year over 2007–2017, a boom the IMF links to public investment in large infrastructure projects. The IMF says the same drive built up imbalances, including an overvalued currency and foreign exchange shortages, and growth slowed to 4.2 percent a year over 2018–2025. The Tigray war of 2020–2022, COVID-19 and drought deepened the slowdown, and income per person growth fell to 2.6 percent in 2022. A reform program launched in July 2024 floated the birr and came with a debt restructuring, and with good harvests, gold and new electricity, growth picked up to 7.0 percent in 2025, when income per person reached its highest level so far.

threads.title: A public investment boom
threads.text: Over 2007–2017 income per person grew 7.3 percent a year. The IMF credits public investment in large infrastructure projects and says the same drive built up imbalances. In the data, investment peaked at 40.7 percent of GDP in 2015 and fell to 20.1 percent by 2025.

citations.title: The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Third Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement, and Financing Assurances Review (IMF Country Report No. 25/188)
citations.quote: Although a key driver of growth was public investment in large infrastructure projects, this contributed to macroeconomic imbalances that threatened to undermine progress.

threads.title: War, pandemic and drought
threads.text: The Tigray war began in November 2020 and ended with the Pretoria peace agreement of November 2022. It came on top of COVID-19, drought and locusts. Income per person growth fell to 2.6 percent in 2022, its lowest since 2003.

threads.title: Floating the birr
threads.text: Before the reform the official exchange rate was held well above its market value, and dollars were rationed. The birr was floated as part of a wider reform program launched in July 2024.

citations.quote: Prior to the FX reform, the significantly overvalued real exchange rate hindered efficient resource allocation by distorting relative price signals, and constrained private sector growth.

threads.title: Debt distress and restructuring
threads.text: Ethiopia missed a Eurobond interest payment in December 2023 and has been in debt distress since. By mid-2026 it had signed bilateral deals with several official creditors and reached an agreement in principle with its Eurobond holders.

threads.title: Gold, power and harvests
threads.text: The recent pickup rests on good rains, more mining, strong gold exports and new electricity from the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam. Income per person grew 4.9 percent in 2024 and 7.0 percent in 2025.

since_last_year.text: Over the past year growth kept speeding up on gold, electricity and farm output, and income per person grew 7.0 percent in 2025, its fastest since 2015. In 2026 the war in the Middle East raised fuel and fertilizer import costs, which the IMF calls a substantial external shock.

citations.quote: Available indicators point to accelerating growth since mid-2024

citations.quote: While strong macroeconomic performance to date has created resilience, the war in the Middle East represents a substantial external shock.

growth_story.tension: The IMF describes fast and accelerating growth in GDP. Income per person grew more slowly: 4.2 percent a year over 2018–2025, down from 7.3 in 2007–2017. The gap is population: a fast-growing population takes a large share of output growth before it reaches income per person.
